preferences.tempo: both slow/atmospheric and fast/plot-driven if well executed
preferences.endings: all types acceptable if well written (twist, emotional, open-ended)
preferences.characterPreferences: multiple types: transformation, strategy, psychology, relationships; do not infer a single dominant type
preferences.storyComplexity: both layered/complex and clear/accessible if well written
preferences.spoilers: none by default; explicit user permission required
preferences.unknownDataPolicy: Never invent unknown ratings, watch statuses, dates, comments, or reasons for a score. Preserve null/unknown.
preferences.ratingScopePolicy: TV series scores are overall series scores unless explicitly season-specific; franchises are overall franchise scores unless explicitly scoped; never distribute a franchise score to individual entries; distinct spin-offs remain separate.
preferences.trueDetectiveS1Limitation: User does not remember why rating was not higher; do not invent a shortcoming.

integrityRules: Never overwrite existing user data without backup and preview.
Perform deduplication by external ID where available; otherwise use normalized title + year + kind and ask/flag ambiguous matches.
Do not create separate film-level ratings from franchise-level ratings.
Keep user rating separate from external/public ratings.
Do not turn explicit liked status into a numerical score unless a scored record already exists.
Preserve unknown year, rating, status, and scope as null/unknown.
Do not create records for titles that are only assistant recommendations unless they are explicitly included in this export.
Import should be idempotent: running it twice must not duplicate records.
Generate a dry-run report before committing changes.
After import, verify record counts and rating distribution.
